This role serves as a shared resource supporting multiple entities across the QC Ecosystem, helping project and program teams maintain visibility into schedule performance, budget status, forecasted outcomes, risks, and overall program health. The Project Controls Manager partners closely with Program Managers, Cost Estimators, project teams, and leadership to ensure programs are built on reliable data, realistic forecasts, and disciplined controls processes. Cost Controls & Forecasting Support budget tracking, forecasting, and performance measurement activities. Monitor cost performance and identify variances against approved budgets and forecasts. Develop forecast-at-completion projections and provide visibility into potential budget outcomes. Partner with Cost Estimators and Program Managers to evaluate financial impacts associated with project changes. Support monthly forecasting and project performance reviews. Risk, Issues & Change Management Partner with Program Managers to maintain risk registers and support risk management processes. Track project risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies across programs. Support risk assessments and mitigation planning activities. Maintain change logs and ensure approved changes are incorporated into schedule and cost forecasts. Provide visibility into emerging risks that may impact project performance. Program Reporting & Analytics Develop and maintain dashboards, reports, and performance metrics that provide visibility into project and program health. Data Integrity & Controls Governance Maintain project controls processes, reporting standards, and performance measurement practices. Ensure consistency, accuracy, and integrity of schedule, cost, and forecasting data. Support development and maintenance of project baselines. Coordinate with project teams and stakeholders to ensure reporting inputs remain current and reliable. Help establish a single source of truth for project and program performance information. Cross-Functional Coordination Partner with Program Managers, Cost Estimators, project teams, and operational stakeholders across the QC Ecosystem. Support project planning sessions, execution reviews, and program governance activities. Facilitate communication between stakeholders regarding schedule performance, forecasting, and program risks. Assist leadership in understanding key program trends, risks, and performance indicators. What Success Looks Like Project schedules accurately reflect execution plans and remain current. Risks, delays, and performance concerns are identified early and communicated proactively. Forecasts provide reliable visibility into potential project outcomes. Leadership receives accurate, timely, and actionable reporting. Cost, schedule, and risk data remain aligned and support informed decision-making. Program teams have confidence in project controls processes and reporting. Governance reviews are supported by accurate, well-organized performance information. Project controls practices improve consistency, accountability, and visibility across the organization. Experience supporting data center, infrastructure, utility, energy, industrial, mission-critical, or large-scale capital construction programs. Strong understanding of project scheduling, cost forecasting, performance measurement, change management, risk management, and program reporting. Experience developing, maintaining, and analyzing project schedules and performance metrics. Working knowledge of Earned Value Management (EVM), including CPI, SPI, EAC, and variance analysis. Experience with Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, project controls platforms, and cost forecasting tools. Ability to develop forecasts, identify trends, and proactively communicate risks and potential project impacts. Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate complex project data into actionable recommendations. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. Ability to work effectively across multiple projects, teams, and business units. Ability to operate in a fast-paced environment while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail. Preferred Qualifications Experience with quantitative risk analysis and contingency planning. Familiarity with schedule quality assessments and DCMA scheduling principles. PMI-SP, PSP, CCP, EVP, PMP, or similar certifications. Physical Demands Duties The following physical demands must be met by the employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Durch unsere Fusion aus Stromnetz Hamburg und Gasnetz Hamburg eröffnen sich dir zahlreiche neue Chancen. Werde Teil unseres Teams, gestalte die Zukunft aktiv mit und profitiere von attraktiven Benefits! Aufgaben Zu deinen Hauptaufgaben gehört die Projektierung von Standard-Hausanschluss-Erneuerungen und kleinen Niederspannungsnetzprojekten – von der technischen Auslegung über die Materialauswahl bis zur Bewertung wirtschaftlicher und technischer Ausführungsvarianten. Du verantwortest den wirtschaftlichen und sicheren Einsatz der dir zugewiesenen Betriebsmittel und wirkst an der Weiterentwicklung von Arbeitsprozessen mit. Als Ansprechperson für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden betreust du Anfragen zur Erneuerung von Netzkabeln und Strom-Hausanschlüssen, stimmst Termine ab, klärst technische Fragen und informierst zu Ablauf und Auswirkungen der Arbeiten. Du planst Kabeltrassen, stimmst dich mit internen Schnittstellen und Behörden ab, berücksichtigst technische und bauliche Rahmenbedingungen und holst erforderliche Genehmigungen und Nutzungsverträge ein. Während der Umsetzung übernimmst du die Bauüberwachung, stellst Qualität, Arbeitssicherheit und Regelkonformität sicher, dokumentierst die Maßnahmen und meldest Abweichungen an die zuständigen Stellen. Außerdem rechnest du die erbrachten Leistungen mit externen Dienstleistenden ab, pflegst die Projektdaten in den IT-Systemen und nimmst am Bereitschaftsdienst teil. Profil Du verfügst über eine Ausbildung als Meisterin (a*) / Technikerin (a*) oder eine vergleichbare Ausbildung. Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Bau elektrotechnischer Anlagen sowie fundierte Erfahrung in Projektarbeit und Projektleitung bringst du bereits mit. Kenntnisse im Mittel- und Niederspannungsnetz sind von Vorteil und erweitern dein Profil. Der sichere Umgang mit gängigen IT-Anwendungen wie MS Office und Power BI ist für dich selbstverständlich, ebenso wie eine ausgeprägte digitale Affinität. Unternehmerisches Denken, ein sicheres und überzeugendes Auftreten sowie eine hohe Engagement Bereitschaft prägen dein berufliches Selbstverständnis. Du überzeugst durch Teamfähigkeit, Organisationsstärke, Durchsetzungsvermögen und Freundlichkeit. Zudem bist du mobil durch einen Führerschein der Klasse B. review_candidates.title: Media designer
review_candidates.description: At Bending Spoons, we’re striving to build one of the all-time great companies. A company that serves a huge number of customers. A company where team members grow to their full potential. A company that functions at unparalleled levels of effectiveness and efficiency. A company that creates value for shareowners at an extraordinary rate. And a company that does so while adhering to high ethical standards. In pursuit of this objective, we acquire and improve digital businesses, not to sell on, but to own and operate for the long term. The transformations we make are often deep—designed to speed up innovation, benefit customers, and strengthen business performance. Here, hierarchy is minimal and teams are small and talent-dense. We operate established products with the ambition, agility, and urgency of a startup. Across the company, we integrate AI deeply into how we work so that human judgment and machine intelligence reinforce each other. For a talented, driven, and collaborative individual, working at Bending Spoons is an opportunity to learn, make an impact, and progress their career at an exceptionally high rate. That’s our promise to such a candidate. A few examples of your responsibilities Create exceptional visual assets across every touchpoint. From paid and organic social content to product visuals, brand assets, and presentation decks, create work that's effective, visually compelling, and delivered fast. Own the quality of every deliverable from brief to final output. Master your craft and raise the bar. Develop deep expertise in your primary discipline: motion, graphic design, illustration, or others. Build skills across adjacent ones to increase the range of work you can own. Stay ahead of what is possible, with AI. Use AI tools to push your creative output further and faster—from generating concepts and exploring visual directions quickly, to accelerating production workflows. Stay ahead of what's possible and apply new techniques where they matter. Deliver at pace, without sacrificing quality. Handle a high volume of work across multiple projects and priorities without dropping below excellent. Make smart trade-offs between craft and urgency. Execute with business awareness. Understand why something is being made, who it's for, and what success looks like. Use that context to make better craft decisions—not just aesthetically stronger ones, but strategically purposeful ones. Spot opportunities and take initiative. Don't wait for a fully formed brief. Flag gaps, propose ideas, and identify moments where proactive creative work can have a real impact—then act on them. What we look for Reasoning ability. Given the necessary knowledge, you can solve complex problems. You think from first principles, and structure your ideas sharply. You resist the influence of biases. You identify and take care of the details that matter. Drive. You’re extremely ambitious in everything you do—and your initiative, effort, and tenacity match the intensity of your ambition. You feel deeply responsible for your work. You hold yourself to a high—and rising—bar. Team spirit. You give generously and without the expectation of receiving in return. You support the best idea, not your idea. You're always happy to get your hands dirty to help your team. You’re reliable, honest, and transparent. Proficiency in English. You read, write, and speak proficiently in English. What we offer Incredibly talented, entrepreneurial teams. You’ll work in small, result-oriented, autonomous teams alongside some of the brightest people in your field. An exceptional opportunity for growth. We go to great lengths to hire individuals of outstanding potential—then, our priority is to put them in the ideal position to thrive. Spooners in their 20s lead products worth hundreds of millions of dollars. And if you’ve got what it takes, you’ll soon be playing an essential role in major projects, too. All. These. Benefits. Flexible hours, remote working, unlimited backing for learning and training, top-of-the-market health insurance, a rich relocation package, generous parental support, and a yearly retreat to a stunning location. We help each Spooner set up the conditions to do their best work. Competitive pay and access to company equity at a discount. Typical annual salary offers range from £56,345 to £85,797 in London and from €54,346 to €82,557 elsewhere in Europe. The lower end of these ranges applies to candidates with little or no relevant experience, while exceptionally experienced candidates may receive offers of up to £196,764 in London or €188,848 elsewhere in Europe. Candidates offered a permanent contract may choose to receive part of their compensation in discounted company equity. Commitment & contract Permanent or fixed-term. Full-time. Location Milan (Italy), London (UK), Madrid (Spain), Warsaw (Poland). The selection process In our screening process, we prioritize verifiable signals of excellence, regardless of seniority. There are no preferential paths beyond what your application demonstrates, and we evaluate every candidate through the same process. Some people hold back because they feel they lack experience or have an “imperfect” CV. If you like the role and believe you could excel over time, don’t self-reject. All applications go through our careers page, which is the only way to be considered. If you pass our screening, you’ll be asked to complete one or more tests. They are challenging, may involve unfamiliar problems, and can take several hours. To learn more about what to expect throughout the selection process, you can find additional information here. We set the bar high and won’t extend an offer until we’re confident we’ve found the right candidate. This is why a job may remain open for months or be reposted several times. We consider all applicants for employment and provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities—please let us know through this form. Before you apply If you’ve applied before but didn't receive an offer, we recommend waiting at least one year before applying again. Bending Spoons is a demanding environment. We’re extremely ambitious and we hold ourselves—and one another—to a high standard. While this tends to lead to extraordinary learning, achievement, and career growth, it also requires significant commitment. To help you ramp up quickly and set yourself up for success, we expect you to spend most days in our Milan office during your first few months with us, regardless of your long-term work location. It’s the best way to rapidly absorb our company culture and build trust with your new teammates. We’ll support you with generous travel and accommodation assistance. After that, you’re welcome to work from one of our offices, or remotely from approved countries—depending on what we agree at the offer stage. If the role speaks to you and you’re excited to give your best, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now—we can’t wait to meet you.

review_candidates.title: Manager, Financial Planning & Analysis
review_candidates.description: POSITION SUMMARY The Manager, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) is a key member of the Finance leadership team responsible for leading Milton Hydro’s enterprise-wide financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and management reporting processes across the regulated utility and its unregulated businesses. Reporting directly to the Vice President, Finance & Chief Financial Officer, the Manager provides financial leadership and business partnership across the organization, ensuring business leaders have timely, meaningful and actionable financial information to support effective decision-making and accountability. The role has primary responsibility for consolidated and business-unit budgeting and forecasting across the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow , with particular emphasis on operating, maintenance and administration (OM&A) expenditures. The Manager works closely with business leaders to develop budgets and forecasts, monitor actual results, understand financial and operational drivers, identify emerging risks and opportunities, and support disciplined management of expenditures. The Manager also supports strategic initiatives, financial modelling, business cases, and transactions involving Milton Hydro's regulated and unregulated businesses. KEY DUTIES Financial Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting Lead the annual budget and periodic forecasting processes for Milton Hydro and its subsidiaries, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives, operating plans and financial targets. Develop and maintain integrated forecasts covering the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow . Coordinate assumptions, timelines and deliverables across Finance and operational business units. Lead financial consolidation of business-unit and subsidiary budgets and forecasts. Support longer-term financial planning, scenario analysis and sensitivity modelling to assess financial outlook, risks and opportunities. Identify emerging financial trends and provide timely updates and recommendations to the CFO and business leaders. Business Partnership & Financial Management Act as a trusted financial partner to business-unit leaders, helping them understand financial performance and effectively manage budgets and expenditures. Provide regular financial updates to business units and business lines, including the regulated utility and unregulated businesses. Lead monthly and quarterly variance analysis against budget, forecast and prior periods, translating results into clear business drivers and management actions. Maintain a strong focus on OM&A expenditure management , working with business leaders to monitor actual and committed spending, forecast year-end results and identify potential pressures or savings. Establish clear financial accountability and provide business leaders with meaningful information to support expenditure and resource decisions. Provide financial analysis and recommendations for operational initiatives, business cases and investment decisions. Management Reporting & Performance Analysis Develop and maintain concise, decision-useful management reporting for the CFO, executive leadership and business-unit leaders. Establish and monitor financial and operational Key Performance Indicators that provide early visibility into performance, risks and opportunities. Improve the quality and consistency of financial reporting across business units, including reporting for regulated and unregulated operations. Support CFO and executive-level reporting and analysis, including financial outlooks and explanations of significant variances. Regulatory & Accounting Support Incorporate applicable Ontario energy regulatory and policy requirements and accounting and tax considerations into budgets, forecasts and financial analysis. Support Finance and Regulatory functions with financial information and modelling required for regulatory planning, applications and other OEB-related activities. Apply knowledge of the OEB Accounting Procedures Handbook (APH) and Modified International Financial Reporting Standards (MIFRS) , where applicable. Work collaboratively with Accounting and the Controllership to ensure appropriate alignment between financial planning, management reporting and reported financial results. Unregulated Businesses, Transactions & Strategic Initiatives Provide FP&A support for Milton Hydro's unregulated businesses, including financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis and management reporting. Support business combinations, acquisitions, investments, divestitures and other transactions , including financial modelling, valuation support, due diligence and assessment of financial impacts. Support integration and post-transaction financial planning and performance monitoring, as required. Develop financial models and business cases for new initiatives and investment opportunities. Provide financial analysis in support of corporate strategy and other priorities led by the CFO. Team Leadership & Process Improvement Lead, coach and develop a small team of financial professionals/specialists. Establish clear priorities, responsibilities and service expectations for the FP&A function. Build strong working relationships across Finance, Regulatory and operational departments. Continuously improve budgeting, forecasting, reporting and analytical processes, with an emphasis on accuracy, efficiency, automation and actionable insight .
